heuristics.rule: Most offers are won at network activation and outreach steps, not at application submission
heuristics.condition: When deciding how to allocate job search time and energy...
heuristics.action: ...spend 50%+ of time on cold outreach, referral requests, and networking with strangers rather than submitting applications
heuristics.because: ATS systems filter out 75-90% of applicants before human review; a referral guarantees human eyes on your resume, which is the actual bottleneck

heuristics.rule: For international students with OPT deadlines, start full-time job search 12-18 months before graduation
heuristics.condition: When you are an international student with visa authorization constraints...
heuristics.action: ...begin company targeting, network activation, and outreach 12-18 months before graduation rather than treating it as a post-graduation task
heuristics.because: Visa timelines compress options; by the time urgency is felt, the best relationship-building windows have already closed

heuristics.rule: The further down the referral priority list you are, the more proof of worth must be in your outreach message
heuristics.condition: When reaching out to someone at a target company with no close connection...
heuristics.action: ...front-load your outreach with concrete evidence of your work and value rather than relying on the connection itself to carry weight
heuristics.because: A cold contact with no obvious common ground has no social obligation to help; demonstrated worth is the substitute for relationship

heuristics.rule: Never ask for a job or referral directly in the first informational interview conversation
heuristics.condition: When conducting an informational interview with someone at a target company...
heuristics.action: ...ask for knowledge, insight, and advice only; let the social relationship develop before any ask
heuristics.because: People are more likely to move your resume after they've met you and feel a relationship exists; premature asks short-circuit that process

heuristics.rule: Your resume is support material, not your search strategy
heuristics.condition: When feeling stuck or unproductive in a job search...
heuristics.action: ...stop optimizing the resume and redirect energy to network activation and direct outreach
heuristics.because: The resume validates an opportunity already created through relationships; it cannot create the opportunity itself

heuristics.rule: Apply to companies you have researched, not companies you have heard of
heuristics.condition: When building a target company list...
heuristics.action: ...include 10-30 companies with explicit rationale based on culture, team, and tech stack research rather than defaulting to brand-name recognition
heuristics.because: Brand-name companies attract disproportionate applicant volume; well-researched lesser-known companies offer better conversion odds and demonstrate genuine fit

heuristics.rule: Networking done 12+ months before you need a job is categorically different from networking at graduation
heuristics.condition: When you still have time before your job search becomes urgent...
heuristics.action: ...begin relationship-building immediately, demonstrating value back to contacts and having authentic low-pressure conversations
heuristics.because: Late networking under pressure is visible to recipients and forecloses reciprocal relationship development; early networking builds the actual asset you'll draw on later

heuristics.rule: Practice interviews out loud, not in your head
heuristics.condition: When preparing for behavioral or technical interviews...
heuristics.action: ...drill STAR responses aloud with another person rather than reading about frameworks or rehearsing mentally
heuristics.because: Interview performance is a distinct physical and cognitive skill separate from knowledge; it requires repetition of the actual act, not study of the concept

decision_factors.why_it_matters: The closeness of your connection to someone at a company determines how much proof of worth your outreach must carry and how likely the referral is to result in human resume review
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map your LinkedIn and personal network against each target company; categorize each contact as close friend, acquaintance, mutual connection, or cold contact

decision_factors.factor: Work authorization timeline and visa status
decision_factors.why_it_matters: For international students, OPT and visa deadlines impose hard constraints on when job search must begin and which companies are viable targets; mismanaging this forecloses options entirely
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Know the exact dates of authorization windows; have a written communication ready to share with recruiters proactively

decision_factors.factor: Planning horizon relative to graduation or OPT deadline
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Starting too late makes Type A high-leverage activities impossible because there is no time to build real relationships before you need them
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Count months remaining before graduation or authorization deadline; if less than 6 months, options are already constrained and strategy must shift

decision_factors.factor: Quality and completeness of portfolio and proof of work
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Demonstrated outcomes rather than experience descriptions are what hiring managers report as distinguishing hired candidates; without published proof of work, outreach and applications lack credibility
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether your resume and portfolio contain quantified outcomes (e.g., reduced latency by 40%) or only activity descriptions (e.g., worked on backend systems)

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Companies in active growth have unlisted roles that get filled before posting, making them accessible through the hidden job market in ways that stable or contracting companies are not
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Track funding announcements and hiring announcements for target companies; prioritize outreach to companies in expansion phases

decision_factors.factor: Specificity of interest in each target company
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Hiring managers consistently identify generic interest as a disqualifying signal; candidates who can reference specific products, tech stack, or recent news convert at higher rates
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Test whether you can articulate a specific reason why this company over a competitor; if you cannot, you have not done sufficient research

decision_factors.factor: LinkedIn profile optimization for recruiter search
decision_factors.why_it_matters: LinkedIn functions as a search engine; inbound recruiter discovery depends on keyword and skill optimization, not narrative quality, creating a distinct optimization target from the resume
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether your headline, skills section, and keywords match the terms recruiters would use to search for candidates in your target role

decision_factors.factor: Recency and depth of interview practice
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Interview performance is a perishable skill built through out-loud repetition; candidates who have not practiced with another person in the last two weeks are measurably underprepared
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check when you last did a live out-loud practice session with another person, not internal mental rehearsal

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Spending most job search time on application submission and resume optimization
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: You are competing in the 10-25% of applicants who survive ATS filtering while simultaneously building no relationships that would bypass that filter; high effort produces low and declining returns
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Students who interpret activity volume as progress and conflate feeling productive with generating pipeline

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Waiting until graduation or near graduation to begin networking
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Every contact you reach out to can detect the pressure and urgency; you are asking for immediate favors from people who have no relationship with you, which dramatically lowers response and conversion rates
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: International students with OPT deadlines, who face the highest time pressure and therefore the most visible desperation signal

hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: You face the highest applicant volume, lowest referral-to-hire conversion, and no differentiation advantage; excellent opportunities at lesser-known companies go unexplored
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Students without existing connections at top-brand companies who rely on cold applications as their primary entry mechanism

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Skipping informational interviews and going straight to formal applications
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: You forfeit inside knowledge about team culture and real requirements, miss unlisted positions, and remove the social obligation mechanism that makes referrals more likely
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Candidates who interpret the informational interview as a low-value social formality rather than a structural advantage in the hiring process

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Practicing interview responses mentally rather than out loud with another person
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: You build familiarity with the content but not the performance skill; the actual interview requires a different cognitive and physical capability that mental rehearsal does not develop
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: High-knowledge candidates who underperform in interviews relative to their actual competence and attribute poor results to nerves rather than insufficient skill-building

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Building a network only when you need something
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: You have no reservoir of weak ties or reciprocal relationships to draw on; the network available at graduation is exactly and only what was built over the prior two years
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Students who treat networking as a transactional job search activity rather than an ongoing professional habit

failure_patterns.pattern: Treating job search as a post-graduation activity rather than a concurrent multi-semester project
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: The urgency of job searching is not felt until graduation approaches; coursework and short-term academic deadlines crowd out longer-horizon career work that has no immediate deadline
failure_patterns.consequence: By the time search begins, 12-18 months of relationship-building time is gone; the candidate is forced into low-leverage cold applications under time pressure
warning_signs: No target company list exists with more than 6 months left before graduation
LinkedIn network has not been activated or expanded since starting the program

failure_patterns.pattern: Defaulting to Type C low-leverage activity (browsing job boards, abstractly optimizing resume) instead of Type A high-leverage outreach
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Type C activity is comfortable and feels productive; Type A requires tolerating rejection and the discomfort of reaching out to strangers, so it is avoided through rationalization
failure_patterns.consequence: Hours invested in job search produce no pipeline; candidate interprets lack of results as a credential or resume problem rather than a strategy problem
warning_signs: Spending more than 2 hours per day on job board browsing with no outreach messages sent
Resume has been revised more than 5 times but no informational interviews have been conducted

failure_patterns.pattern: Generic application strategy with no company-specific preparation
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Casting wide feels like it increases odds; researching each company deeply before applying feels like inefficient effort allocation when applying to many companies
failure_patterns.consequence: Hiring managers identify the candidate as generically interested rather than specifically motivated; fail to get offers despite strong credentials
warning_signs: Cannot articulate a specific reason for wanting to work at any given company beyond its reputation
Cover letters and interview answers do not reference specific products, teams, or recent company news

failure_patterns.pattern: Strong credentials but inability to explain work clearly and concisely
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Technical candidates optimize for doing the work rather than narrating it; the skill of explaining work in 90 seconds to a non-technical audience is never practiced
failure_patterns.consequence: Fails to convert interviews to offers despite having the underlying competence; hiring managers interpret poor explanation as a signal about collaboration and communication fit
warning_signs: Cannot explain most impactful project in under 90 seconds in a way a non-technical person would find compelling
Has never practiced 'tell me about yourself' out loud with another person

failure_patterns.pattern: Treating rejections as noise rather than diagnostic data
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Rejection is emotionally aversive; analyzing it requires re-engaging with a negative experience, so candidates move on without extracting learning
failure_patterns.consequence: The same failure modes repeat across multiple application cycles with no improvement in conversion rate
warning_signs: Has received multiple rejections at the same stage (e.g., consistently failing phone screens) without changing preparation approach
Has never requested feedback after a rejection or tracked which stage rejections are occurring at

diagnostic_questions.question: Can you explain your most impactful project in 90 seconds in a way that would make a non-technical hiring manager want to know more?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate has translated their technical work into communicable outcomes, and whether they have practiced the actual performance skill of narrating their work
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you practiced this out loud with another person in the last two weeks, or only rehearsed it mentally?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Is the gap a lack of impactful projects, or a lack of practice articulating projects that do exist?

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you have a specific reason why you want to work at each company you are applying to, or are you casting wide?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate is in a generic broadcast strategy or a targeted research-driven strategy; distinguishes candidates who will convert interviews from those who will not
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you spoken to at least one current employee at each of those companies in the last 6 months?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: How many of the companies on your list have you done substantive research on beyond reading their about page?

diagnostic_questions.question: What is the exact timeline of your work authorization status, and have you communicated it clearly to recruiters?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate has a clear grip on their visa constraints and whether those constraints have been proactively surfaced to recruiters, or whether they are being hidden or ignored
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have any recruiters screened you out based on visa status, and if so, are you targeting companies known to sponsor?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: How many months remain before your authorization deadline, and does your current search timeline account for that?

diagnostic_questions.question: How are you allocating your job search time across outreach and networking versus application submission versus research and resume work?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate is investing in high-leverage Type A activities or defaulting to comfortable low-leverage Type C activities; surfaces whether the strategy matches the mental model
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: How many cold outreach messages or informational interview requests did you send in the last two weeks?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: What is preventing you from doing more direct outreach — discomfort, lack of contacts, or uncertainty about how to approach it?

diagnostic_questions.question: When did you begin building your network and target company list relative to your graduation or authorization deadline?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate is in the early-networking compounding phase or the late-networking desperation phase; determines which strategies are still available to them
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you been able to demonstrate value back to contacts over that time, or has the relationship been one-directional?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Given the compressed timeline, which high-leverage activities should be prioritized immediately to recover as much relationship runway as possible?

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you practiced behavioral interview questions using STAR format out loud with another person in the last two weeks?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate understands that interview performance is a perishable skill requiring active maintenance, or whether they believe knowledge of the framework substitutes for practiced execution
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What feedback did you receive, and what have you adjusted based on it?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Are upcoming interviews in your pipeline, and if so, what is the plan to build that skill before those interviews occur?

industry_realities.common_belief: Submitting more applications increases your odds of getting a job
industry_realities.actual_reality: ATS systems filter out 75-90% of applicants before any human sees the resume; volume of applications without relationship activation produces diminishing and eventually near-zero returns
industry_realities.implication: Effort should be reallocated from application volume to referral acquisition and network activation, which bypass the ATS filter entirely

industry_realities.common_belief: A referral gives you a significant advantage in the hiring process
industry_realities.actual_reality: A referral does not guarantee a job — it guarantees a human review of your resume; the value is specifically in bypassing automated filtering, not in preferential hiring treatment
industry_realities.implication: A referral is necessary but not sufficient; the resume and interview performance must still be strong enough to convert once human review occurs

industry_realities.common_belief: Job searching is something you do after graduation or when you need a job
industry_realities.actual_reality: The network available at graduation is the one built over the previous two years; relationship-building done under time pressure converts at far lower rates than early-stage relationship-building
industry_realities.implication: Job search must be treated as a concurrent multi-semester project, not a post-graduation event

industry_realities.common_belief: The hidden job market is inaccessible without insider connections
industry_realities.actual_reality: The hidden job market is most accessible through weak ties — acquaintances met at conferences or events often have more novel information than close friends in the same industry — and through targeting companies in active growth phases where unlisted roles exist
industry_realities.implication: Weak tie cultivation and tracking funding and hiring announcements are practical, actionable entry points to unlisted roles

industry_realities.common_belief: LinkedIn is primarily a place to post your professional history for hiring managers to read
industry_realities.actual_reality: LinkedIn functions as a search engine; recruiter discovery is driven by headline keywords and skills sections, not narrative quality; optimization must target the recruiter search query, not the hiring manager read
industry_realities.implication: LinkedIn profiles require two distinct optimizations: keyword and skills density for inbound discovery, and narrative quality for post-discovery conversion

industry_realities.common_belief: Studying interview frameworks like STAR prepares you for behavioral interviews
industry_realities.actual_reality: Reading about STAR and drilling STAR out loud are completely different skills; interview performance requires the physical and cognitive habit of speaking coherently under pressure, which only repeated out-loud practice with another person builds
industry_realities.implication: Interview preparation must include live out-loud practice sessions with real feedback, not just content review or mental rehearsal

industry_realities.common_belief: Applying to well-known brand-name companies is the safest and highest-probability strategy
industry_realities.actual_reality: Brand-name companies attract disproportionate applicant volume, making cold applications the least efficient use of search effort; excellent companies that candidates have never heard of offer better conversion odds when combined with proper research
industry_realities.implication: Target company lists should be built on research and fit rationale, not name recognition; including lesser-known companies with active growth and research depth often yields better outcomes

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: Core mental model of how jobs are obtained
junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Treats job search as a volume game: send many applications, wait for responses, get lucky through persistence
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Treats job search as a relationship activation problem: build pull within target companies, convert relationships to interviews, use application as validation step not discovery step
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: The mental model determines time allocation; junior model produces mostly Type C activity, senior model produces mostly Type A activity with structurally higher conversion rates

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: Where in the hiring funnel effort is concentrated
junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Starts at the application step, treating resume submission as the primary activity
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Starts at company identification and network activation, treating application as a late-funnel confirmation of an opportunity already created
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Most offers are won at steps 2-4 of the funnel; starting at step 5 means competing only among those who bypassed the relationship layer entirely

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Treats rejection as failure or bad luck; moves on without extracting learning or adjusting strategy
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Treats rejection as a filtering mechanism and diagnostic data; asks for feedback, tracks which stage rejections occur at, and adjusts approach accordingly
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Candidates who analyze rejections improve their conversion rate over time; those who do not repeat the same failure modes across multiple cycles

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: Timing of network-building relative to job need
junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Begins networking when job search urgency is felt, typically at or near graduation
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Builds network continuously, starting 12-24 months before any job need, treating it as an ongoing professional habit rather than a transactional search activity
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Early networking produces authentic relationships with compounding value; late networking is detectable as desperate and converts at far lower rates

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Describes activity and experience: 'worked on backend systems,' 'contributed to the data pipeline'
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Describes outcomes and impact: 'reduced latency by 40%,' 'cut data pipeline failure rate by half in Q3'
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Hiring managers consistently report outcome framing as a distinguishing signal; activity descriptions are interchangeable across candidates while outcome descriptions are specific and credible

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Targets companies by name recognition and reputation; applies broadly to well-known brands
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Targets companies by researched fit: culture, tech stack, team, growth stage, and specific rationale for why this company over alternatives
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Research-based targeting produces specific and credible interest signals that hiring managers identify as differentiating; brand-name targeting produces generic interest that is explicitly cited as a disqualifying pattern

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Studies interview frameworks and reviews content mentally; believes knowing STAR is equivalent to being able to execute it
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Drills responses out loud with another person repeatedly; treats interview performance as a physical skill requiring repetition, not content knowledge requiring study
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Interview performance under pressure requires a built habit of coherent verbal expression; mental rehearsal does not develop that capability and leads to underperformance relative to actual competence
